name: nanopb
listed_description: Small code-size Protocol Buffers implementation in ANSI C.
reason: Project goal is code size, not speed: its docs index lists 'Some speed has been sacrificed for code size' and give only absolute code-size figures (5-20 kB) with no named baseline. The only measurements reachable were third-party and show nanopb slower than a rival: the SofaBuffers arena README reports nanopb at 125,240 msg/s versus protobuf-c at 663,929 msg/s, and compares its own codec against nanopb for footprint (nanopb 6,612 bytes on Cortex-M). The author's own 2015 comparison page (jpa.kapsi.fi/nanopb/benchmark) is blocked from this session (EGRESS_BLOCKED) and is described as out of date.

name: PackedArray
listed_description: Random-access array of tightly packed unsigned integers of any desired width. Has a SIMD-optimized implementation.
reason: Repo benchmark directory holds PACKEDARRAY_SELF_BENCH output for Core i7 M620, iPhone 5, iPad 2 and Galaxy Note, but each file compares only the project's own reference, unrolled and SSE2/NEON pack/unpack code against memcpy and a plain uint32_t loop copy used as context rows; no claim of beating an incumbent container (std::vector, uint32_t array) and no numbers against one. The README's only figure is a worked memory example (17 bits versus 32 bits, a 47% overhead for uint32_t), not a measurement.

name: pal
listed_description: Optimized library for maths, parallel processing and data
reason: README states 'Fast' as a design goal and links a status page (parallella.github.io/pal-stats, blocked from this session) but contains no timings. The benchmark/ directory (benchmark.c, runbench.*.c, math and image subdirectories) only times PAL's own functions (p_add_f32, p_sqrt_f32, p_sincos_f32 and similar) and defines no libm, glibc or other baseline to compare against.
